title: Repository Traceability, Determinism, and Security Governance
authorityBoundary: This artefact defines repository governance and future validation expectations for traceability, deterministic outputs, security scanning, vulnerability scanning, reproducible builds, and drift detection. It does not implement scanners, tests, validators, generators, runtime code, generated clients, CI workflows, or readiness claims.

checkableNow.description: Future implementation surfaces can be required to reference a semantic definition, accepted ADR, validator requirement, proof requirement, or explicit owner-approved blocker.
Generated clients or schema-derived surfaces can be checked for references to active, draft, or planned schema lifecycle state without promoting planned schemas to active.
App-surface components, generated clients, view models, and route plans can be required to reference app-surface semantic artefacts before implementation is accepted.

semanticImplementationTraceability.futureFailureMode: Future implementation validation must fail closed when an implementation surface lacks semantic authority, invents missing semantics, or maps to a planned schema as though it were active.
semanticImplementationTraceability.readinessBoundary: Traceability planning does not authorise implementation and does not claim generated-client, product UI, staging, production, or live-provider readiness.

requiredReferences: validator rule or planted-defect identifier where applicable
proof requirement or evidence class where applicable
Linear issue identifier for work tracking only
non-claim boundary when the test is readiness-adjacent

reportingFormat.antiTheatreRule: A test must not be counted as requirement coverage unless the referenced requirement is actually exercised or intentionally checked as a negative control.

testRequirementTraceability.futureValidationExpectation: Future implementation must demonstrate traceability for representative tests before using traceability reports as acceptance evidence.

scannerScopes.purpose: Detect committed secret-shaped values, private keys, credentialed URLs, API tokens, and unsafe endpoint tokens in repository text, workflow files, generated reports, and evidence artifacts.
scannerScopes.candidateScanner: secret-pattern scanner compatible with the existing environment-tooling secret-like leakage model
scannerScopes.failureMode: fail-closed for likely real secrets; require owner review for allowlist entries and known synthetic fixtures

scannerScopes.purpose: Check that configuration and evidence output use secret references, redacted values, and value-free audit metadata.
scannerScopes.failureMode: fail-closed when secret values are exposed or secret references are replaced by raw credentials

scannerScopes.purpose: Check package dependencies for advisory posture without claiming vulnerability clearance.
scannerScopes.candidateScanner: pnpm advisory audit posture recorded by the supply-chain test gate
scannerScopes.failureMode: record findings and owner decisions; do not expose secrets in logs

scannerScopes.purpose: Check Compose image dependencies where image inventory exists.
scannerScopes.candidateScanner: owner-selected container image scanner after image pinning and provenance posture are settled
scannerScopes.failureMode: defer unsupported scans rather than fabricating pass evidence

allowlistProcess: Allowlist entries require path, finding class, reason, owner, expiry or review date, and evidence that the value is synthetic or intentionally public.
Allowlist entries must not include raw secret values.
Expired, unknown, or ownerless allowlist entries fail closed.
ownerDecisionPoints: deciding severity thresholds that block CI
promoting scan results into acceptance evidence
securityAndSecretScanningProposal.futureProofExpectation: Future implementation must prove synthetic secret fixtures are detected and real secret values are not printed, committed, or persisted.

dependencyVulnerabilityScanProposal.dependencyOnSecurityScanProposal: Satisfied by securityAndSecretScanningProposal in this artefact.

scannerScope.outputBoundary: advisory report or deferred evidence without secret exposure
scan result, deferred unsupported scope, or owner blocker

severityThresholds.defaultAction: block future acceptance until remediated, deferred with owner decision, or proven not applicable
require owner review, remediation plan, or bounded exception before acceptance
record remediation flow and review cadence
record posture without upgrading readiness claims
fail closed for pass claims and require owner review

remediationFlow: identify affected dependency, image, or transitive component
record source input and scan evidence
decide update, pin, exception, deferral, or removal
rerun relevant validation after future implementation changes
preserve non-claims until evidence supports stronger posture
dependencyVulnerabilityScanProposal.futureValidationExpectation: Future implementation must report scan results without exposing secrets and must not treat advisory absence as functional correctness.

currentBlockers.description: Generated reports, bundles, proof cockpit artifacts, and future build outputs may contain timestamps, run identifiers, or source paths that need explicit normalization policy.
Outputs may vary by Node or package-manager version, OS path behaviour, locale, timezone, cache state, or hidden local state.
Generated clients are semantic definitions and future outputs only; no generated-client implementation exists in this planning scope.

proofNeededBeforeCachingBuildOutputs: content hash for inputs and outputs
fallback to full rebuild on missing or unknown provenance
reproducibleBuildExpectations.futureValidationExpectation: Future implementation must compare independent builds and explain all differences before build outputs can be cached as proof-supporting artifacts.

requirements: timestamp fields isolated from semantic comparison
deterministic ordering of operations and fields
no behaviour not found in USF authority
no package publishing or implementation readiness claim
content-addressed or hashed outputs where available

deterministicGeneratedOutputRequirements.intentionalVariancePolicy: Future generators must identify any expected variance field and exclude it only from equivalence comparison, not from evidence custody.
deterministicGeneratedOutputRequirements.futureValidationExpectation: Future implementation must prove regenerated outputs are stable or explain intentional variance without hiding meaningful behaviour or proof differences.

driftClasses.description: A doc, generated report, test, validator, or tool references an obsolete, missing, lower-authority, or inactive authority source.
A future implementation or generated client lacks semantic authority or changes behaviour not backed by semantic definitions.
Docs, agent directives, CI, package scripts, Make targets, or proof instructions disagree about a command, alias, or compatibility target.
A generated output no longer matches source authority, declared inputs, generator expectations, or staleness state.
Evidence, generated reports, or human decisions remain treated as current after semantic definitions, source SHA, input hashes, provider mode, or environment changed.
Security scan posture, secret boundary, vulnerability posture, allowlist ownership, or advisory evidence falls behind current dependencies or workflows.

severityLevels.ownerAction: block pass or completion claims until authority, evidence, or validator posture is corrected or owner-approved as deferred
require issue-level review, remediation plan, or documented deferral before depending on the affected surface
record and schedule cleanup without upgrading readiness claims

validatorCandidates: evidence freshness and source SHA checker
scan posture and allowlist ownership checker
driftDetectionDesign.futureValidationExpectation: Future implementation must include planted drift fixtures and fail-closed behaviour before drift detection can be treated as enforced.

currentNegativeControls.currentRole: Existing validators and planted defects prove known forbidden states fail closed.
Existing drift cases cover missing command, stale generated output, missing contract mapping, and readiness overclaim.
Existing planted cases cover tool-version drift, command mismatch, generated-artifact drift, private-state leakage, secret-like leakage, missing environment boundary, and unsupported overclaim.

gaps.description: A generated report, implementation surface, or Linear issue implies authority over semantic definitions.
A hermetic or test proof is treated as live-external-provider, staging, production-shaped, or production-live proof.
A stale, unknown, missing, or generated-only evidence record is accepted as pass.
A planned schema or contract is consumed as active without lifecycle promotion and validator coverage.

prioritizedAdditions: provider-mode and environment upgrade planted defects
missing traceability planted defects for future implementation surfaces
negativeControlDesign.futureValidationExpectation: Future implementation must prove each negative control fails for the intended reason and must not count a negative case as covered unless its authority reference is explicit.

scenarios.expectedResult: pass only for dev-level proof; fail for composed service or staging claims
pass only for Test or Compose proof; fail for staging, production-shaped, production-live, or live-external-provider claims
fail when evidence freshness is stale, unknown, or mismatched to the source input set
fail for live-provider or staging claims unless separately authorised and evidenced

environmentSimulationTestDesign.futureValidationExpectation: Future implementation must prove simulated evidence cannot satisfy higher proof levels and must keep simulation labels distinct from live-provider, staging, production-shaped, and production-live evidence.

auditScenarios.expectedFailClosedBehaviour: A staging-style proof claim fails when Dev and Test prerequisites are missing or stale.
A mock, hermetic, or local-composed provider proof fails when used as live-external-provider proof.
Evidence without provider-mode labels fails instead of defaulting to pass.
Evidence without environment labels fails instead of inheriting environment from command or path.
A generated report cannot satisfy proof without underlying raw evidence and source input references.
A low-risk documentation or routing change must not be forced into staging proof unless its risk classification requires it.

proofLadderAuditTestDesign.futureValidationExpectation: Future implementation must include failing fixtures for incorrect proof promotion and must preserve current proof gates rather than relaxing them.

blockedItemsNotClosed.reason: Validator property-based tests remain blocked by validator regression-proofing before UI work.
